newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends day little changed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends day little changed.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market ended Friday's session unchanged, getting an early start on next week's holiday-shortened week.
Municipals were holding steady despite some deterioration at the long end of the Treasury market. The government long bond was down 8/32 at 100-26/32 to yield 6.44 percent.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed up 3/32 to 117-23/32 and December T-bonds were 7/32 lower at 115-10/32. The MOB spread was 77 ticks, widening from 67 at the close Thursday.

In the muni secondary, bids on Cook County, Ill., FGIC 5-7/8s of 2022 were unchanged at 100-7/8. Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, Ill., AMBAC 5-1/4s of 2027 were down two basis points to 5.64 percent.
"It's all over until 10 days from now," one market analyst said, referring to next week's holiday week, when few deals are expected to price.

Underwriters priced about $4 billion of new deals this week, but only about $352 million of deals are slated for pricing over the Thanksgiving holiday week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $233.8 million in 38 issues. The largest is a $39.4 million Newark, N.J., deal on November 26.
Negotiated sales total $117.9 million in 11 offerings for the week. The largest is a $23 million Lincolnton, N.C., issue through Robinson-Humphery Co.
